findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:244 — The `flusher_unhealthy` metric reuses the tag key `"shard"` but here binds it to a single shard int per iteration, whereas `main()` (line 185/195) binds the same key `"shard"` to a comma-joined string of all shards for a process — the same tag name carries different types/semantics depending on call site, which will confuse anyone querying or dashboarding this metric.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:244 — The `flusher_unhealthy` metric reuses the tag key `"shard"` but here binds it to a single shard int per iteration, whereas `main()` (line 185/195) binds the same key `"shard"` to a comma-joined string of all shards for a process — the same tag name carries different types/semantics depending on call site, which will confuse anyone querying or dashboarding this metric.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is only emitted in `_ensure_processes_alive()` with tags `{ "cause": ..., "shard": shard }` where `shard` is an int from the loop over `shards`. `main()` does not emit `flusher_unhealthy` at all; it tags other metrics/timers (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`) using `shard_tag` (comma-joined string) and uses a different tag key (`"shards"`) for `wait_produce`. So the finding’s claim that the same metric (`flusher_unhealthy`) uses the same tag key with different semantics across these call sites is not supported by the diff.
